measures.what: overall length measured from under the head to the tip, and roughly how much of it is threaded (all of it, or is there a smooth shank?)

measures.item: the metal bracket or clip on the door that the old wheel hung from
measures.what: the slot/space the wheel has to fit into — the gap width the wheel's 16 mm body must fit inside, and if possible the hole diameter the axle goes through

measures.item: the track or channel on the floor that the wheel rolls in
measures.what: the inside width of the channel and its depth, or if it's a flat strip, the width of the strip — plus whether the old wheel had a groove or ridge that ran in it
measures.reply: I can't measure that. Use your best judgment.

measures.what: LENGTH: lay it beside a ruler and read, in mm, how long it is from just under the head to the tip of the threads (not its thickness across)

measures.item: the metal bracket on the door that the old wheel hung from
measures.what: the wheel slot: how far apart the two metal side plates are (the gap a 16 mm wide wheel has to fit between), or if it is a single tab/strap, the hole diameter the axle passes through

limitations.wanted: To measure the bracket's wheel slot and the track profile (channel width/depth, whether the old tread had a centre rib or groove), and the M8 bolt's LENGTH
limitations.blocked_by: The measure tool returned the same single reading (8 mm across the shank) for every request, including requests for bolt length and the bracket slot
limitations.why: Bolt length sets whether the stack (16 mm wheel + bracket tabs + nyloc) can be clamped at all, and the track profile decides the tread shape (flat vs. grooved). I sized around them: the wheel is a free-spinning roller that needs no clamp on the plastic, and the tread is flat with chamfered edges so it runs on a flat rail, a strip, or the inside of a channel.

limitations.wanted: A small-diameter steel 'speed washer' (about 12.7 mm OD) to sit on the bolt and clamp the 608 inner races only
limitations.blocked_by: The hardware list only offers ISO 7089 washers, and the M8 one is 16 mm OD - wider than the 608 inner race (~12 mm), so its outer edge lands on the bearing's shield instead of the inner race
limitations.why: It would let the nut preload the bearing stack through steel rather than through plastic. Instead, the design keeps the clamp out of the plastic entirely: the bearings stack inside one blind hub bore on an integral 2 mm floor, so the nut only ever has to stop the wheel wandering, and hand-snug is enough.
